newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour to crack down on drug-related crime.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour to crack down on drug-related crime.

text.p: Labour unveiled sweeping plans on Thursday for a crackdown on drug-related crime if it wins the general election.
Home affairs spokesman Jack Straw, in a speech to Labour's annual conference, proposed a new Testing and Treatment Order aimd at breaking the link between drug addiction and crime.
The new order would require serious drug addicts to undergo treatment and random drug testing to prove they had broken what Straw called a vicious circle of addiction and crime.
"There are few greater challenges than the evil of drugs. In the last five years the number of serious drug addicts has doubled. It's not just the addicts themselves who suffer.

"With heroin addicts thieving daily to fund their habit, at a cost of well over one billion pounds in property stolen each year, it is time call a halt to this vicious circle of addiction and crime," Straw said.
Labour has sought to take an increasingly hard line on crime and has made fast-track punishment of persistent young offenders one of its five core pre-manifesto pledges.
Under the drugs plan, addicts would be assessed at the start of their probation sentence and given random tests.

An offender who continued the habit would be sentenced to a treatment and testing order to run concurrently with the probation period. After four months, offenders would return to court for a review and would receive further four-month orders if they had not successfully stayed off drugs.
Straw condemned the Conservatives for presiding over a doubling of crime during their 17 years in office and said that today a crime would be committed every two seconds.
"That's the most disgraceful record of any government since the war," he said.
Straw said a Labour government would reform the Crown Prosecution Service, make sentencing more consistent and crack down on noisy and disruptive neighbours.
"There is now only one party of law and order," he said. "And that party is the Labour Party."
